s: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to
o: solve the problem of minorities in India
give effect to the Independence Bill
delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan
enquire into the riots in East Bengal
x: The Radcliffe Line was the boundary between the Indian and Pakistani portions of the Punjab Province and Bengal Presidency of British India. It was named after Cyril Radcliffe, who served as the joint chairman of the boundary commissions for the Punjab and Bengal provinces. The demarcation line was published on 17 August 1947 upon the Partition of British India. Today, its western side is part of the India–Pakistan border, while its eastern side is the Bangladesh–India border.

s: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to –
o: Solve the problem of minorities in India
Give effect to the Independence Bill
Demarcate the boundaries between India and Pakistan
Enquire into the riots in East Bengal
x: Viceroy of British India, Lord Mountbatten formed two commissions namely Punjab Border Commission and Bengal Border Commission to decide the borderline between India and Pakistan on June 30, 1947 AD. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as President of both the Commissions. Those Commissions had to demarcate borders by Muslims and Non-Muslims population. They had to consider other factors too. There were four members (judges) in each Commission of which two were from Indian National Congress and two from the Muslim League.

s: President of Indian National Congress at the time of Independence was?
x: J. B. Kripalani was the President of Indian National Congress at the time of Independence. Elected in November 1946 A.D. at Meerut Session, Acharya (scholar) Jivatram Bhagwandas Kripalani was a Gandhian Socialist, environmentalist, mystic and freedom fighter and was noted for his incorruptibility and determination. Kriplani was prominently involved over a decade in top Congress party affairs and the organization of the Salt Satyagraha and the Quit India Movement.

Congress Socialist Party (1934) *In May 1934, the All India Congress Committee met at Patna to set up a Congress Parliamentary Board to fight elections under the aegis of Congress itself. However, some of the members of All India Congress Committee held separate meetings and founded All India Congress Socialist Party, and this party was officially inaugurated in October 1934 A.D. The policies and working methods were to be decided in a meeting that was to be held in Bombay. *Jaya Prakash Narayan was the convener of All India Congress Socialist Party in Patna, 1934. He was the general secretary of party and Acharya Narendra Dev was the President. The objective of the was to push the Indian National Congress towards a clear socialist agenda, focusing on full independence, abolition of landlordism and nationalisation of key industries. Who advocated 'Neo-Buddhism'?
x: Neo-Buddhism was name given to Dalit Bauddha Movement started by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Under this, Buddhism was redefined and new Buddhist sect 'Navayan' was founded.

s: Who advocated ‘Neo-Buddhism’?
x: Navayana/Neo-Buddhism means "new Vehicle" and refers to the re-interpretation of Buddhism by B.R. Ambedkar. Navayana rejects practices and precepts such as renouncing monk and monasticism, Karma, rebirth after life, samsara, meditation, enlightenment and four noble truths considered to be foundational in the Buddhist traditions. It revises the original Buddha's teachings about class struggle and social equality.
